scope: Representative original-period construction with declared normal-use operation, not a verified individual building. All thermal grades and catalogue source records are retained. Source stock means are acceptance comparisons, not layer recipes or solved thicknesses.

source_locators.scope: Source stock means have no layer recipe. The selected timber/ceiling/slab recipe is a declared representative construction, with fixed existing thermal grades and no reverse U-value solving.

tabula.selection: Original U-values are synthetic BETSI stock means. All accepted benchmark values, locators and 20% tolerance remain unchanged.

wall.history_scope: Bjerking R106:1978 pp39–40/Fig2222b supports the cross-framed mineral-wool/windboard/gypsum family from 1965; it specifies 50 mm nominal cross-members, not this 70 mm selection. Use the same existing 70 mm nominal composite layer for both later eras as an explicit engineering default. No exact historical product or construction drawing is claimed.
wall.dimension_context_scope: Svenskt Trä guidance published 2003 supports insulated inner framing dimensions 45–70 mm in its timber construction examples. This is later buildability context, not proof of the exact 1988 wall or a substitute for the period family source.
wall.renovation: Reuse accepted shared 45/70 mm facade-wool plus 22 mm panel additions outside the complete retained nominal core. The source prescribes nominal added depth and a panelled finish; grade/panel dimensions are explicit EPSM defaults.

attic.scope: Both later eras use the same 300 mm nominal original ceiling (200mm framed+100mm continuous) with unchanged historic wool. This is a declared completion default in the documented over-joist family. Geometry follows the accepted 75/c1200 family; 15% is replaced by the stated field-framing geometry, not tuned separately by era. Bjerking p43 illustrates c600, so adopted spacing/depths remain explicit engineering defaults.
attic.period_context: Energimyndigheten ET2009:19 p11 gives 1986–2004 approximate original attic U .15 and wall U .20; these provide context, not layer prescriptions or changed acceptance targets.
attic.period_locator: Bjerking R106:1978 printed p43/Fig2234: continuous mineral-wool mat above insulated framing; adopted exact depths/spacing are engineering defaults.
attic.renovation: Retain the original and reuse shared 200/500 mm loose-wool additions, with unchanged Supafil EPD reference. Source capture remains in evidence/sf_se02_source_review.json#/carbon_review/loft_epd.

floor.source_recipe: Retain user-stack nominal under-slab EPS and 120 mm slab; replace 10 mm timber finish with 40 mm bonded cement finish. The source is evidence/sfh_baseline_user_stacks.txt, P05 for 1988 and P06 for 2000. Finish and exact depths are EPSM representative choices, not recovered TABULA layers.
floor.renovation: Retain all baseline mineral layers; add 40/45 mm warm-side EPS at lambda 0.036 plus 50 mm floating mineral cement finish. Floor rise 90/95 mm; shared Generic HW Concrete is a thermal/concrete-family carbon proxy.
floor.boundary: Soil-facing slab on ground. Nominal material-layer U is distinct from effective ground U; soil, geometry, ground method, moisture, load distribution, reinforcement and clearances remain project inputs.

windows.selection: Retain existing baseline and standard definitions; advanced reuses the accepted TABULA replacement. Original nominal optics remain an EPSM lumped assumption rather than a claim to reproduce TABULA glazing g and frame separately.

validation: Independent organized fixture cases/sf_se05.json stores fixed source values and declared nominal geometry. Thermal checks run forward. No benchmark tolerance was widened; missing carbon modules and project quantities remain missing.
limits: Original facade cladding,battens and cavity quantities remain project inputs; windboard thermal proxy/asphalt content and retained-stock carbon are not exact historic products.
All thermal material/source records and all benchmark values/tolerances remain unchanged.
No actual individual building or structural/fire/moisture certification is claimed.
